limitations: Two once-started callers, each selecting append, replacement or deletion. One exclusive lease with one token per caller; any number of modeled expirations before callers settle. One task and its listing index.

The primary task mutation and lease-token comparison are one Redis command. Listing zadd/expire/zrem remain separate operations with possible failure and lag. Index repair, pagination completeness and tenant/index migration are outside this instance.

Real implementation checks use a single loopback Redis server and explicit synchronous memory backend. Redis Cluster cross-slot support, failover, acknowledged-write durability, unknown transport outcomes, arbitrary concurrent clients, task semantic policy and downstream provider effects remain outside this proof.

Conformance executes eight named real-store scenarios. It is not a generated-trace refinement proof. Foreign read/update/delete refusal is tested but cross-tenant noninterference across all methods is not proved.
